meta.title: Portolan — An opinionated standard for cloud-native geospatial catalogs
meta.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files on object storage, with no servers, no databases, and no proprietary licenses. Structured metadata lets both people and AI agents read a catalog, understand it, and query it directly. The standard sets the quality bar, a validator enforces it, and a set of tools makes catalogs cheap to build and easy to use.

nav.tagline: An opinionated standard for cloud-native geospatial catalogs.

hero.title: The future of spatial data
hero.description: Portolan is an opinionated standard for sharing geospatial data as cloud-native files on object storage, plus the tools that make it real. A Portolan catalog is a directory of open-format data described by structured <m>STAC</m> metadata, hosted on any S3-compatible bucket. No servers, no databases.

why.title: The job of an SDI has changed.
why.subtitle: Spatial data infrastructure still assumes servers, databases, and specialists. Portolan doesn't.

open.title: Open and interoperable
open.description: Everything is open source under <m>Apache-2.0</m> and built on existing standards like <m>GeoParquet</m>, cloud-optimized GeoTIFF, and <m>STAC</m>. These formats work across DuckDB, BigQuery, Pandas, and desktop GIS like QGIS and ArcGIS, so your data works everywhere, with or without Portolan.

aiFirst.title: Readable by people and machines
aiFirst.description: Older tooling like WFS and Shapefiles was built for one client at a time. A Portolan catalog describes itself in plain text and structured metadata, so a person, a script, or an agent can find the data and query it without a bespoke API to learn. The <link>Finland.SDI demo</link> shows an agent doing exactly that against a national SDI.

easy.title: Simple
easy.description: Traditional spatial data infrastructure needs databases, services, and staff to run them. A Portolan catalog is files in a bucket. Point the CLI at your data, convert, and push.

scalable.title: Scales with your storage
scalable.description: The same setup handles megabytes or terabytes. There are no servers to run, so scaling is your cloud provider's job, not yours.

lowCost.title: Low cost
lowCost.description: The whole budget is storage plus egress. Sharing public data should not take an operations team, and a popular dataset should not blow a budget. The <link>cost calculator</link> shows what your data would run.

sovereign.title: Sovereign
sovereign.description: The full stack can live inside your own jurisdiction. Host on AWS, GCS, Azure, MinIO, Hetzner, Scaleway, or any S3-compatible storage. No foreign vendor sits between your agency and its data.

howItWorks.title: Point, convert, push.
howItWorks.subtitle: A shared set of open formats replaces the server. Cloud storage does the scaling. Browsers, query engines, and AI agents read the files directly.

convert.title: Convert
convert.description: Convert shapefiles, GeoTIFFs, WFS, GeoPackage, and ArcGIS Feature Services into cloud-native formats. Vectors become <m>GeoParquet</m>, rasters become <m>COG</m>, and map tiles become <m>PMTiles</m>.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: Generate a <m>STAC</m>-based catalog that describes every asset with structured metadata. Any <m>STAC</m> tool can read it.

publish.title: Publish
publish.description: Push the files to any S3-compatible object storage. That includes AWS, GCS, Azure, R2, MinIO, and Source Cooperative for free open data hosting.

browse.title: Browse
browse.description: Open the catalog in the Portolan browser or any STAC viewer, query it with DuckDB, or point an agent at the URL. The data answers questions directly.

ecosystem.title: All of it is on GitHub.
ecosystem.subtitle: The standard defines what a great catalog is. The validator proves it, the CLI builds it, and the browser and registry make it easy to find and use. Each part raises the value of the others, and all of it is <m>Apache-2.0</m>.

quickstart.title: Publish your first catalog.
quickstart.intro: Start by browsing a live catalog. Then publish your own with the CLI or with an agent.

browse.title: Browse a catalog
browse.description: Portolan catalogs are live on the web. Open the browser to explore published datasets, or point DuckDB at any <m>GeoParquet</m> URL and query it in place.

cli.title: With the CLI
cli.description: Install <m>portolan-cli</m>, then <m>init</m>, <m>add</m>, <m>check</m>, and <m>push</m>. The CLI converts your files and generates the catalog.

claude.title: With Claude
claude.description: Install the Portolan skill in Claude Code and point it at your data. It handles conversion, metadata, and publishing. Agents excel at CLIs and text files, so non-experts can publish too.
